descriptionChirho: A large group of people, whether a nation's populace, an army, or a gathered assembly. Used extensively in the historical and prophetic books to describe masses of people in military or civic contexts (Judg 4:7, 1 Sam 14:16, 2 Sam 6:19, 1-2 Kings, 2 Chronicles, Ezekiel, Daniel). Arabic jumhur ('crowd, throng'), Korean muri ('multitude'), Hindi bhir ('crowd'), Spanish multitud consistently confirm the sense of a large human gathering.

Noisy disturbance or upheaval, often the din of a crowd, a battle, or social disorder. Distinguished from mere 'noise' by the element of chaotic human agitation: the tumult in the Philistine camp (1 Sam 4:14, 14:19), the confusion of a battlefield (2 Sam 18:29), the commotion of nations (Isa 13:4, 17:12, 33:3), and prophetic visions of cosmic upheaval (Jer 3:23, Ezek 23:42, Dan 10:6). Arabic dajij ('commotion'), Korean soran ('disturbance').

A large quantity or great amount of material possessions, resources, or things (not people). Used of the abundance of nations promised to Abraham (Gen 17:4-5), the wealth prepared for the temple (1 Chr 29:16), riches better than which is the little of the righteous (Ps 37:16), the futility of wealth (Eccl 5:10), and the abundance of possessions in prophetic judgment oracles (Jer 49:32, 51:42). Arabic kathrah ('abundance'), Hindi bahut ('much'), Korean pungseongham ('abundance').

An audible sound such as the roaring of waters, the rumbling of an approaching force, or a loud clamor. Distinct from 'tumult' in that the focus is on the acoustic phenomenon itself rather than social disorder: the sound of heavy rain (1 Kgs 18:41), the noise of waves (Ps 65:7), the roar of enemies (Isa 31:4), the sound of the fall of Tyre (Ezek 26:13), and the noise of judgment (Jer 47:3, Amos 5:23). Arabic dajij/hafif ('noise'), Korean soran/sori ('noise/sound'), Spanish estruendo/ruido ('din/noise').
